question_text: Which countries make up the United Kingdom?

options.text: England, Wales, Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man
England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland

options.rationale: These three make up Great Britain, not the whole UK.

explanation_simple: The UK is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
memory_tip: Great Britain is the big island; the UK adds Northern Ireland.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Is the following statement TRUE or FALSE? Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom.
explanation_simple: Northern Ireland is one of the four countries of the UK, with England, Scotland and Wales.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Which countries make up Great Britain?

options.text: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
options.rationale: That is the United Kingdom, not Great Britain.

explanation_simple: Great Britain means England, Scotland and Wales. The UK is Great Britain plus Northern Ireland.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Is the following statement TRUE or FALSE? Northern Ireland is part of Great Britain.
explanation_simple: Northern Ireland is part of the UK but not of Great Britain, which is England, Scotland and Wales.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: What is the full official name of the country?

options.text: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
Great Britain and the British Isles
The United Kingdom of England and Scotland

explanation_simple: The official name is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Is the following statement TRUE or FALSE? The Isle of Man is part of the United Kingdom.
explanation_simple: The Isle of Man and the Channel Islands are Crown dependencies. They are closely linked to the UK but are not part of it.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Which TWO of these are Crown dependencies, closely linked to the UK but not part of it?
explanation_simple: The Channel Islands and the Isle of Man have their own governments and are not part of the UK.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Which of these statements is correct?

options.text: The Channel Islands and the Isle of Man have their own governments.
The Channel Islands and the Isle of Man are governed directly by the Scottish Parliament.

explanation_simple: The Crown dependencies have their own governments, though they are linked to the UK.

source.reviewer_note: CHECK FIRST: Confirm the handbook names the Falkland Islands and St Helena as examples. Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Which of these is a British overseas territory, linked to the UK but not part of it?
explanation_simple: British overseas territories, such as the Falkland Islands and St Helena, are linked to the UK but are not part of it.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Where does the UK Parliament sit?
explanation_simple: The UK is governed by the Parliament sitting in Westminster, London.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Is the following statement TRUE or FALSE? Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own parliaments or assemblies with powers over some matters.
explanation_simple: Some powers are devolved: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own parliament or assemblies that decide some matters for themselves.

source.reviewer_note: Confirm the section heading wording in the handbook

question_text: Which of these statements is correct?

options.text: The Republic of Ireland is not part of the United Kingdom.
The Republic of Ireland is part of the United Kingdom.

explanation_simple: Ireland is divided: Northern Ireland is part of the UK, while the Republic of Ireland is a separate country.
